standard.title: Evaluation of Completed Irrigation Projects (Major and Medium) — Guidelines (पूर्ण हो चुकी सिंचाई परियोजनाओं (प्रमुख एवं मध्यम) का मूल्यांकन — मार्गदर्शी सिद्धांत)
standard.sector: Water Resources / Irrigation Planning and Management

sectional_committee.name: Water Resources Planning, Management and Evaluation Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard provides guidance for carrying out the performance evaluation of completed major and medium irrigation projects, with a special emphasis on the irrigation component, and also outlines evaluations for socio-economic, agro-economic, environmental, ecological, hydropower, navigational, and flood protection impacts.

certification.description: Voluntary Guidelines. Since IS 16115:2013 is an evaluation guideline and methodology standard rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its data collection scales, map requirements (e.g., 1 : 250 000 scale), and performance benchmarking is widely enforced and mandated by the Central Water Commission (CWC), the Ministry of Jal Shakti, and state irrigation departments during post-project performance audits, renovation proposals, or modernization (ERM) funding evaluations. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Specifies that the scope of the project as revised during execution and finalized at the completion stage must be taken as the base. Original or revised project reports must serve as the technical basis for comparison during performance evaluations.

Notes that comparison with original target reports may not always reflect true performance because annual inflows or physical water availability may differ widely from those projected during planning, requiring adjustments.

Requires evaluating completed irrigation projects across multiple dimensions, including socio-economic, agro-economic, environmental, ecological, hydropower generation, navigational, and flood protection aspects.
Mandates collecting detailed primary data for the overall command area (per Clause 8.2 to 8.7) to support comprehensive macro-level evaluations.

Specifies map scale requirements: an index map on a scale of 1 : 250 000, command maps showing the canal network and major drainages, soil survey maps, and maps of tube wells and groundwater observation wells (recommending a 1 : 250 000 scale).
Requires analyzing key operational constraints in the canal network to identify specific structures or channels that need to be remodeled, or new works that must be provided.
Mandates evaluating user and operational attitudes, including cooperation among farmers and officials, and the overall attitude of the farmers toward the project.
Requires conducting a macro-level performance study of the existing irrigation system to benchmark system efficiencies, water delivery timelines, and agricultural productivity.
